text:
maria: quick sync — ran the multi-pop latency sweep for the new int8 quant LlamaX variant across us-east / us-west / eu-west. pushing raw numbers and a tiny summary below.

maria: results (p50 / p95 / throughput @ 2048 tokens):
- us-east (h100, kernel auto): 42ms / 160ms / 320 qps
- us-west (h100, kernel auto): 46ms / 175ms / 290 qps
- eu-west (a100, kernel fallback): 58ms / 240ms / 260 qps

maria: notable: eu-west shows both higher p50 and fat tail at p95. suspect kernel fallback + higher hop counts from edge routing.

kai: nice. did you include prefix cache warmup? how many warmup reqs?

maria: yes — 1000 warmup requests per pop, then steady-state 30m at 2.5 RPS per client. numbers above are steady-state after cache warmed. also toggled continuous batching on for h100 runs.

noah: can you drop the per-region kernel decision log? want to see where it fell back.

maria: pasted kernel log snippet:
```
2026-03-19T14:01:02Z local: selected kernel=h100-optimized-v3
2026-03-19T14:01:02Z eu-west: selected kernel=a100-fallback-llamax-v1 (quant path uses slower matmul)
```

maria: infra-bot: rendered latency chart https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/rows/9876?range=last_6h
infra-bot: (chart) https://console.redwood.ai/snapshots/59934

samantha: @maria can you sanity check networking path? eu-west p95 jump looks like an extra 25-40ms egress hop vs us-east.

maria: confirmed via traceroute: eu-west edge -> internal-proxy -> model-host (2 extra hops) avg added 22ms.

derek: kernel fallback + extra network hop = compounding. two levers: pin a100 kernel variants (tune GEMM) or route EU traffic to us-east h100 for latency-critical customers.

kai: throughput numbers for a100 were similar-ish but tail worse. what's the RPS headroom for eu-west if we pin kernels?

maria: quick capacity calc:
- current: 260 qps (a100) @ 1 shard per 8g workload
- tuned kernel estimated +18% throughput -> ~307 qps
- routing to h100: ~320 qps but network cost + egress >+12% latency variance depending on POP

noah: do we have perf regression risk after quant? any quality diffs on eval set?

maria: small quality delta on long-context hallucination metric (~0.6% increase). need to run eval harness with longer prompts. flagged in evals board: https://console.redwood.ai/evals/board/llamaX-int8-2026

samantha: for customers with strict p95 SLOs, recommend temporary routing policy:
```
policy:
  route_preference: local-first
  fallback_to: nearest-h100
  kernel_pin: true
```

maria: created a canary run with that policy for 2 hours starting in 15m. will post updated numbers.

derek: also add a quick smoke to measure p99 tail with synthetic spike (10x RPS for 30s) — we saw tail amplification on EU hosts earlier.

maria: ack. running spike smoke at 2350001180

infra-bot: canary deployed -> route-policy=eu-local-pin -> canary-id=cp-2350001122

maria: quick interim numbers after 10m canary:
- eu-west pinned kernel + route local: 48ms / 170ms / 300 qps (p95 dramatically improved)

kai: solid. looks like kernel pin was the dominant factor; routing helped a bit.

noah: next steps: 1) full eval on long-context quality 2) bake kernel optimization for a100 (small GEMM tweak) 3) update routing policies for SLO tiers

samantha: I'll draft a short runbook for on-call: what to flip if eu-west p95 creeps beyond 200ms.

maria: thanks all. will upload final sweep CSV and perf traces here once run completes: s3://redwood-inference/bench/2350001122/
